This holds the implicit assumptions (with commentary):

  • Your minority employees have an equal say in the user-facing design of your products (as opposed to reality where usually a small number of product designers design the product and everyone else works to spec)

  • Suitably skilled candidates from a wide range of backgrounds will apply for roles you advertise (this usually will not be the case)

  • It's possible to design your product to appeal to a wide range of minority demographics without compromising appeal for your majority user base (appealing to a wide range of different minority demographics will require a large number of different and possibly conflicting changes to your product)

  • There's a positive return on investment from targeting said minority demographics (by definition they're a small market when taken as a group, and the further you specialise for smaller, more specific demographics the worse your ROI will get.)
